plt.figure(figsize=(8, 4))

ax1 = sns.countplot(x='hotel', hue='is_canceled', data=df)

ax1.legend(labels=['Not Cancelled', 'Cancelled'], bbox_to_anchor=(1, 1))

plt.title('Reservation Status in Different Hotels', size=20)
plt.xlabel('Hotel')
plt.ylabel('Number of Reservations')

plt.show()

We notice that City hotel has more bookings and cancelletions than resort ones, maybe because resort hotels are more expensive. The city hotel must keep track of the cancellation ratio and address the reason behind the cancelletions.

In [35]:
resort_hotel= resort_hotel.groupby( 'reservation_status_date')[['adr']].mean()
city_hotel= city_hotel.groupby( 'reservation_status_date')[['adr']].mean()
In [36]:
plt.figure(figsize =(20,8))
plt.title('Average Daily Rate in City and Resort Hotel (ADR)',fontsize = 30)
plt.plot(resort_hotel.index,resort_hotel['adr'],label= 'Resort Hotel')
plt.plot(city_hotel.index,city_hotel['adr'],label= 'City Hotel')
plt.legend(fontsize= 20)
plt.show()

City hotels appear to have a moderate ADR, and as expected, their prices are lower than those of resort hotels. This could contribute to the higher number of bookings observed for city hotels. However, resort hotel rates may increase on specific days, such as weekends and holidays, which could further affect booking patterns.

In [37]:
df['month'] = df['reservation_status_date'].dt.month
plt.figure(figsize = (16,8))
ax1 = sns.countplot(x='month',hue = 'is_canceled',data = df)
plt.ylabel('Number of Reservations')
plt.legend(['Not cancelled','Cancelled'])
plt.show()

Findings January has the highest number of cancellations. August has the lowest number of cancellations among all months, while also having the highest number of reservations. December has fewer reservations compared with other months of the year.

These patterns may be related to pricing. During December and January, higher prices could make customers more likely to cancel their reservations. In contrast, lower prices in August may contribute to the higher number of bookings observed during this month.

In [43]:
plt.figure(figsize=(15,8))
plt.title('ADR per Month', fontsize=30)
df_filtered = df[df[ 'is_canceled'] == 1].groupby('month')[['adr']].sum().reset_index()
sns.barplot(x= 'month',y= 'adr', data= df_filtered)
plt.show()

The bar chart demostrates that cancellations increase as accommodation prices increase. Therefore, higher accommodation prices may be a significant factor contributing to cancellations.

Direct           0.104696
Corporate        0.042987
Complementary    0.006173
Aviation         0.001993
Name: proportion, dtype: float64

The results prove our hypothesis wrong, as most reservations come through Online Travel Agents (47%), followed by Offline Travel Agents (20%) and Groups (16%), while direct bookings account for almost 10% of cancellations.

The results indicate a higher cancellation rate compared to booking rate, with ADR being the most influential factor contributing to cancellations. As noted earlier, marketing campaigns should therefore be adjusted and personalized based on regional characteristics.

Suggestions:

1.The prices of the hotel are positive related to cancellations rate. Therefore we must focus on better pricing strategies in specific hotels based on the regions. 2.On weekend and holidays days the resorts could provide more resaonable prices for the rooms , in order to prevent the large amount of cancellations during those days 3.In January we could offer discount prices and focus on marketing stategies in order to attract more visitors , which lead to less cancellations and better revenue. 4.We could invest in better facilities in the hotels that are located in Portugal in order to prevent the big persentage of cancellations, which affect the hotels revenue.
